The database schema named 'rschema_0515' consists of six tables: User, Bike, Trip, Malfunction, User_trip, and Use_bike.
The User table is used to store user information, including their credit status, phone number, and verification code. The User table has a primary key composed of the phone number column.
The Bike table is used to store information about bikes, including their ID, status, location information, QR code, and unlock password. The Bike table has an integer primary key, Bike_ID, and a foreign key, User_phone_number, referencing the User table.
The Trip table is used to store information about trips, including the bike ID, end time, fee, payment status, start time, trip ID, and user phone number. The Trip table has a foreign key, Bike_ID, referencing the Bike table and a foreign key, User_phone_number, referencing the User table.
The Malfunction table is used to store information about malfunctions, including the bike ID, malfunction description, report time, and user phone number. The Malfunction table has a primary key composed of the user phone number, bike ID, and report time, and foreign keys referencing the Bike table and the User table.
The User_trip table is used to store information about which trips a user has taken, including the user phone number and trip ID. The User_trip table has a foreign key, User_phone_number, referencing the User table and a foreign key, Trip, referencing the Trip table.
The Use_bike table is used to store information about which bikes have been used in which trips, including the bike ID and trip ID. The Use_bike table has foreign keys, Bike_ID and Trip_ID, referencing the Bike and Trip tables respectively.
All columns allow null values except for the ones that are marked NOT NULL. Default values are not specified for any columns. The database follows referential integrity constraints by using foreign keys to link related tables together.
gold_question: This is a bike-sharing management system. For user management, the system records basic information for each user, including unique phone number, verification code, and credit status. After registration, users can view available bikes nearby. For bike management, the system records basic information for each bike, including unique bike ID, QR code, unlock password, location information and bike status. For trip management, when users obtain the unlock password by scanning QR code or manually entering the code, the system unlocks the bike and starts recording the trip, including start time, end time, riding trajectory and other information. During the ride, the bike periodically uploads location to update trip information. After users end their trips, the system automatically calculates fees based on billing rules and records payment status. Users can view their trip list and detailed information, and can also report bike malfunctions. Merchants can manage bike information, set billing rules, monitor bike status, malfunctions and trips, and manage user credit and status.
ddl:
-- Schema for database: rschema_0515
CREATE TABLE `User` (
  `phone_number` varchar(15) NOT NULL,
  `credit_status` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `verification_code` varchar(10) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`phone_number`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `Bike` (
  `Bike_ID` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `status` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `location_info` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `qr_code` varchar(100) DEFAULT NULL,
  `unlock_password` varchar(50) DEFAULT NULL,
  `User_phone_number` varchar(15) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Bike_ID`),
  CONSTRAINT `Bike_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`User_phone_number`) REFERENCES `User` (`phone_number`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `Trip` (
  `trip_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `Bike_ID` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `User_phone_number` varchar(15) DEFAULT NULL,
  `start_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `end_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `fee` decimal(10,2) DEFAULT NULL,
  `payment_status` varchar(20) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`trip_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `Trip_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`Bike_ID`) REFERENCES `Bike` (`Bike_ID`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `Trip_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`User_phone_number`) REFERENCES `User` (`phone_number`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `Malfunction` (
  `User_phone_number` varchar(15) NOT NULL,
  `Bike_ID` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `report_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `malfunction_description` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`User_phone_number`, `Bike_ID`, `report_time`),
  CONSTRAINT `Malfunction_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`User_phone_number`) REFERENCES `User` (`phone_number`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `Malfunction_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`Bike_ID`) REFERENCES `Bike` (`Bike_ID`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `User_trip` (
  `User_phone_number` varchar(15) DEFAULT NULL,
  `trip_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`User_phone_number`, `trip_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `User_trip_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`User_phone_number`) REFERENCES `User` (`phone_number`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `User_trip_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`trip_id`) REFERENCES `Trip` (`trip_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `Use_bike` (
  `Bike_ID` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `Trip_ID` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`Bike_ID`, `Trip_ID`),
  CONSTRAINT `Use_bike_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`Bike_ID`) REFERENCES `Bike` (`Bike_ID`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `Use_bike_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`Trip_ID`) REFERENCES `Trip` (`trip_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
